subject.name: Mathematics
subject.overview: ICSE Class 8 Mathematics strengthens number work and introduces more formal algebra and geometry. The number chapters cover rational numbers, exponents with negative powers, squares and square roots, and cubes and cube roots. Commercial arithmetic applies percentages to profit, loss, discount, and simple and compound interest. Algebra covers operations on expressions, standard identities and solving linear equations in one variable, including word problems. Geometry and mensuration deal with polygons and quadrilaterals, areas of trapeziums and polygons, and surface area and volume of solids. The year ends with data handling (frequency tables, graphs, mean, median and mode) and an introduction to probability of simple events.
studyTips: Practise prime factorisation until it is quick; it is the fastest route to square roots, cube roots and simplifying exponents.
In profit, loss and discount problems, write CP, MP and SP separately before calculating, and remember that profit or loss percent is on the cost price.
When an equation has fractions, multiply every term by the LCM of the denominators first, then check the answer by substituting it back.
Keep a formula list for areas, surface areas and volumes, and always write the unit (cm², m³) with the final answer.

chapters.name: Rational Numbers
chapters.summary: Studies properties of rational numbers, their operations, inverses and representation on the number line.

topics.name: Rational numbers on the number line

chapters.name: Exponents
chapters.summary: Extends the laws of exponents to negative integral powers and uses them to simplify expressions.

chapters.name: Squares and Square Roots
chapters.summary: Covers properties of perfect squares and finding square roots by prime factorisation and division.

chapters.name: Cubes and Cube Roots
chapters.summary: Covers perfect cubes and finding cube roots by prime factorisation.

chapters.name: Percent and Percentage
chapters.summary: Converts between fractions, decimals and percentages and solves problems on percentage increase and decrease.

chapters.name: Profit, Loss and Discount
chapters.summary: Applies percentages to cost price, selling price, marked price, discount and profit or loss.

chapters.name: Simple and Compound Interest
chapters.summary: Computes simple interest and compound interest for whole numbers of years and compares them.

chapters.name: Algebraic Expressions
chapters.summary: Covers terms, coefficients and the addition, subtraction and multiplication of polynomials.

chapters.name: Linear Equations
chapters.summary: Solves linear equations in one variable, including those with fractions, and applies them to word problems.

chapters.name: Understanding Shapes
chapters.summary: Studies polygons, their interior and exterior angles, and properties of quadrilaterals.

chapters.name: Mensuration
chapters.summary: Finds areas of trapeziums and polygons and surface areas and volumes of cubes, cuboids and cylinders.

chapters.name: Data Handling
chapters.summary: Organises data into frequency tables and graphs and computes mean, median and mode.

chapters.name: Probability
chapters.summary: Introduces experiments, outcomes and events, and the probability of simple events.

questions.text: A fair die is rolled once. The probability of getting an even number is ____.
Find the square root of 5184 by prime factorisation.
An article marked at ₹1200 is sold at a discount of 15%. If the shopkeeper bought it for ₹850, find the profit percent.
questions.explanation: Profit percent is always calculated on the cost price.

questions.text:
A sum of ₹10,000 is invested for 2 years at 10% per annum.
(a) Find the simple interest.
(b) Find the compound interest, compounded annually.
(c) Find the difference between them.
questions.explanation: The difference is the interest earned in year 2 on the first year’s interest (10% of ₹1000).

questions.text: The coefficient of x² in 3x³ − 5x² + 7 is ____.

A father is three times as old as his son. After 12 years, he will be twice as old as his son.
(a) Form a linear equation for this situation.
(b) Find their present ages.
(c) How many years ago was the father five times as old as his son?
questions.answer:
(a) Let the son’s present age be x years; the father’s age is 3x years. After 12 years: 3x + 12 = 2(x + 12).
(b) 3x + 12 = 2x + 24 ⇒ x = 12. Son = 12 years, father = 36 years.
(c) Let it be t years ago: 36 − t = 5(12 − t) ⇒ 36 − t = 60 − 5t ⇒ 4t = 24 ⇒ t = 6. Six years ago (father 30, son 6).

questions.text: Each exterior angle of a regular octagon measures:
questions.explanation: Exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°, so each = 360° ÷ 8 = 45°.

questions.text: Find the area of a trapezium whose parallel sides are 12 cm and 8 cm and the distance between them is 5 cm.
questions.answer: Area = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height = ½ × (12 + 8) × 5 = 50 cm².

questions.text: A room is 6 m long, 4 m wide and 3 m high. Find the cost of painting its four walls at ₹25 per m² (ignore doors and windows).
questions.answer:
Area of four walls = 2h(l + b) = 2 × 3 × (6 + 4) = 60 m².
Cost = 60 × 25 = ₹1500.
